newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine, British ministers to discuss fishing rights.
newsitem.headline: Argentine, British ministers to discuss fishing rights.

text.p: Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella Wednesday departed for London for a new round of talks with his British counterpart Malcom Rifkind on fishing in disputed South Atlantic waters.
Foreign Ministry sources said the visit would be unofficial and Di Tella would fly back home on Thursday.

The two sides, which fought a 10-week war in 1982 for control of the Falkland islands, have since resumed friendly ties, clinched a deal on possible joint oil exploration, and started discussing fishing rights in the sorrounding waters.
But the fishing talks proved thornier than both sides had expected and several rounds of negotiations have produced no visible results.

Last March Argentina decided to suspend the talks after Britain began demanding fishing licenses for Argentine trawlers operating around the South Georgias, near the Falkland archipelago. The issue was then settled and talks resumed.
Although it lost the war, Argentina still claims sovereignty over the islands it calls Malvinas and fears that the payment of licenses could be interpreted as a recognition of British rights.
